newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins track US Treasury, Brady bond rise.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins track US Treasury, Brady bond rise.

text.p: Russian MinFin bond prices firmed on Thursday tracking higher U.S. Treasuries and Brady bonds and dealers said rumours, quickly denied, that President Boris Yeltsin's chief-of-staff Anatoly Chubais had resigned, failed to spoil the market's upward mood.

They added fears about Yeltsin's health were moving to the backstage for the market. The Kremlin issued no immediate news of Yeltsin's health on Thursday, although the Kremlin said a medical bulletin was due after 1300 GMT.
"Prices started rising in the morning, then edged down but are going up again. People seem tired of rumours and are looking more at market factors," an International Moscow Bank dealer said.
Dealers said a rise in U.S. Treasuries and Bradies was the main positive factor for MinFins. The market largely ignored the rumours Chubais had quit, denied by Chubais' press office.
"MinFins are pretty bullish as the trend is better in U.S. Treasuries. Besides the market feels Yeltsin's health is improving," Eurobank dealer Olivier Coursault said.
